title: How Is Bread Made? (You Asked) 🍞 #Shorts
description:
How is bread made? @Ducksonic12 asked, so here it is. Bread isn't fluffy because bakers pump air in. Yeast, billions of tiny living cells, eat the sugar in flour and burp out carbon dioxide gas plus a little alcohol. Kneading links two flour proteins into gluten, a stretchy net that traps the gas like a thousand tiny balloons. In the oven the gas swells one last time (oven spring), the yeast die around 140°F, and the gluten and starch set, freezing the bubbles in place. Most of the alcohol bakes off and becomes part of that fresh-bread smell. Every hole in your toast is a frozen burp.

Explained in 60, podcast edition. Comment what we should explain next.
